newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gene-soya protestors target German seed crushers.
newsitem.headline: Gene-soya protestors target German seed crushers.

text.p: German activists on Wednesday planned to stage a demonstration against genetically altered U.S. soybeans, a statement from organisers BUND, the German branch of environmentalists Friends of the Earth, said.
The group planned to target the stall of Bonn-based German seed crusher organisation VDO during the livestock industries exhibition "EuroTier" which runs from November 12 to 15.
The activists were planning to display banners with anti-soya and anti-VDO slogans.
The statement said VDO mills had a key function in processing soybeans into 80 percent of meals for animal feed and oils for food products such as margarine.
But they refused to separate the new beans from conventional ones and to press for labelling of the products.
Consumers would be "force-fed" the undesirable organisms through meat and dairy products from animals fed on soymeal.
The protest is the latest in a ten-week wave of Europe-centred action against the beans, which make up two percent of this year's U.S. soybean crop.
Campaigners say humans and the environment could be harmed by the products.
VDO members, who last year used 3.4 million tonnes of imported soybeans, have no plans to alter processing schedules.
